name: range()
what_it_does: Generates a sequence of numbers, most often used to control how many times a for loop runs.
syntax: range(stop) or range(start, stop) or range(start, stop, step)
parameters: start (optional) - first number, defaults to 0. stop - one past the last number generated (stop itself is never included). step (optional) - how much to increase each time, defaults to 1 (can be negative to count down).
return_value: A range object - a memory-efficient sequence of numbers, most often looped over directly rather than converted to a list.
common_mistakes: The classic off-by-one error: range(5) produces 0,1,2,3,4 (5 numbers), NOT including 5 - forgetting this leads to loops that run one time too few or too many. range(5, 0) with no negative step produces nothing (empty), since it can't count upward from 5 to 0.
when_to_use: Repeating an action a specific number of times, or generating index numbers to loop over (though enumerate() is usually cleaner when you also need the actual items, not just the index).
